    Offer comparison

    Interview prep

    The follow-up is where most hunts are won.

    Recruiters juggle hundreds of applications. A short, polite follow-up 7 days after applying — and again at 14 — puts your name back on top of the pile. HuntBoard watches the calendar so you don't have to.

    Guides that actually help

    Plain-language playbooks for the moments that decide a hunt.

    01

    The 7-day follow-up

    Short, polite, one screen. Never apologise for following up — you're helping them close a loop.

    • Subject: following up — <Role> application
    • One line: who you are, when you applied
    • One line: why you're a fit, in their words
    • Ask: "Is there anything else you need from me?"
    02

    Before the interview

    Preparation beats talent when talent doesn't prepare.

    • Read the job post again; note the 3 must-have skills
    • One story per skill, with a number in it
    • Know their product — try it, or watch a demo
    • Prepare 3 questions that show you did homework
    03

    Reading an offer

    CTC is not salary. Check what actually lands in your bank.

    • Fixed pay vs variable — variable is not guaranteed
    • Joining bonus: is it clawed back if you leave early?
    • Notice period and bond, if any — read the fine print
    • Compare monthly in-hand, not headline CTC
    04

    After a rejection

    A "no" now is often a "not yet". Leave the door open.

    • Reply within a day, thank them, ask for feedback
    • Ask to be considered for future roles
    • Note what to improve — then move the card on
    • Never burn the bridge in writing
    05

    Salary talk, simply

    Let them name a range first when you can. Then anchor honestly.

    • Know the market range for the role and city
    • Quote a range, not a single number
    • Count the whole package: PF, insurance, perks
    • Get the final offer in writing before resigning
    06

    Keep the hunt honest

    Your applications are a record of what you can actually do.

    • Only claim skills you can demonstrate
    • Never claim a degree or certificate you don't hold
    • One tailored resume per role beats ten generic ones
    • Track every application — memory is not a system
